needs_result.text: Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.
Managed AWS account governance for the project, including root-user isolation, IAM user and group management and least-privilege policies.

Carried it into production with the client's engineering team: contributed to their production TypeScript/Node.js MCP server (OpenAI-based query generation, Convex), now in live use, and reviewed pull requests in the client's production repository alongside their CTO.
Built NLP and agentic RAG workflows with Hugging Face Transformers, Ollama, LangChain and LangGraph.
Built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system (Claude API, LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) served through a FastAPI REST API in Docker on GCP Cloud Run.
Built e-commerce and ticketing UIs in Swift/SwiftUI with product search, cart logic, order tracking and booking management.

Shipped features in a production fintech (financial-services) application as part of a team: integrated Twelve Data (real-time market feeds) and Plaid (bank linking, transaction imports) via REST APIs, with SSL pinning and AWS Cognito SSO.

Needed a voice assistant that answers in real time and can be interrupted: built it end to end as a full-stack application (React front end, FastAPI and Google ADK back end, full-duplex WebSocket) with ReAct-based agent orchestration, barge-in handling and self-hosted speech models on Docker/CUDA (float16 inference, model warm-up) to cut latency.

bullets.text: Needed an agent that researchers could trust on a cancer research platform, including when its tools fail: built a tool-calling agent (LangChain, Claude Haiku 4.5 on AWS Bedrock) for three use cases (gene alias resolution, prompt-engineered explanations of a fixed scoring pipeline, validated dataset descriptions), with deterministic Ensembl and HGNC calls, deterministic hallucination guards, and circuit breakers with a 19,213-gene parquet fallback for when the external APIs are unavailable.

Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.

Wrote a three-tier test framework (tool-level, API/integration, live agent) of ~65 tests across 8 files, validated across the LLM provider migration from Groq to AWS Bedrock after a rate-limit evaluation.

Diagnosed where it struggled with a three-tier, ~65-test evaluation harness (tool-level → API → live) and hallucination-rate analysis, debugging failures layer by layer, and used the same harness to validate the Groq to Bedrock migration after a rate-limit evaluation.

bullets.entry: CoverFit — insurance benchmarking API (Bristol × UWE AI Hackathon)
bullets.text: An insurance sponsor needed a fast, low-cost, explainable benchmark (hackathon brief): paired a deterministic matching engine (FastAPI, pandas, Pydantic) with a single LLM call (Gemini via LiteLLM) for the rationale, covered by pytest tests; responses arrive in under 3 seconds at ~£0.003 per query.
Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.
Proposed and prototyped an MCP-based agentic tool in Python (FastMCP, Ollama gpt-oss:20b, PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions CI), presented in a live stakeholder demo.

Contributed the MCP implementation to the client's production repository (TypeScript/Node.js MCP server, OpenAI query generation, Convex database), now in live day-to-day use; engagement received a 5-star commendation from senior leadership.

A product-startup client needed an agentic AI prototype turned into software their team could use: led the architecture for a five-person cross-functional team, designed hierarchical agent workflows (MCP, Exograph GraphQL, PostgreSQL for persistent storage and retrieval across agent sessions) and built the Python prototype (FastMCP, Ollama, GitHub Actions CI), then ran a live demo with client stakeholders (5-star rating from senior leadership) within the three-month engagement.

Proposed the request flow: a user's text goes through the API and a customised prompt to the MCP server, where one LLM instance writes GraphQL queries against the client's Convex database and a second instance runs the statistical analysis before the result returns to the user.

draft_body: I built production AI services on AWS, packaging them in Docker containers and deploying them with AWS Lambda under precise IAM policies. I designed agentic architectures that let autonomous agents act safely, and I created evaluation pipelines that log metrics and trigger debugging cycles. Each release passes a suite of tests before reaching production, ensuring reliability across the cloud stack. The pipelines also capture context and tool use data to inform continuous improvement, and support rapid iteration of new features.

At AstraZeneca I owned the evaluation and debugging pipeline, delivering roughly 65 tests that validated tool resilience. At 180 Degrees Consulting Bristol I owned the client-facing agentic prototype architecture, coordinated cross-functional teams, integrated agent, MCP, GraphQL and PostgreSQL components with Python, and established CI pipelines, refined tool use within the agent harness, and ensured smooth migration, while maintaining high performance, and documented the architecture for future teams, ensuring scalability and reliability, earning a 5-star rating from senior leadership.

Juro's Agentic team builds the AI foundations the rest of engineering ships on — starting with Operator, the agent that works across contracts inside Juro, and enables faster agreement for users globally.
